data.title: Treasury Yields End Month With Large Declines — Market Talk
data.description:
1619 ET - Treasury yields end October sharply lower as a flight to safety turns September's historic selloff into a bond-buying spree. Binance's $6.3 billion heist spooks equity investors already wary about massive investment in AI. Attention now turns to midterms on Tuesday and the Treasury quarterly refunding plans to be announced Wednesday. Investors will watch for indications of how quickly the Treasury plans to reduce long-term debt issuance in favor of short-term bills. The 10-year yield falls 0.364 percentage point in October, to 4.928%, its largest monthly decline since December 2023. The two-year sheds 0.306 point to 4.579%, its largest one-month drop since August 2025. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1543 ET - Earnings per share growth from five of the "Magnificent 7" companies has so far lagged other names in the S&P 500 Index in the third quarter, per FactSet earnings analyst John Butters. Nvidia and Apple have yet to report their most recent earnings, but the estimated blended earnings growth rate for the group of megacap tech stocks has fallen to 22.6% from 33.6% a month ago, Butters says. That compares with a 32.6% blended growth rate for the other 493 companies in the index, meaning Mag 7 earnings growth is on track to fall below the rest of the index for the first time since the fourth quarter of 2022. Surveyed analysts expect the trend to hold in the fourth quarter this year.(elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1419 ET - Days after raising its policy rate by a quarter point, the Bank of Canada faces a reality check over its outlook for accelerating growth, says David Rosenberg, head of market-strategy firm Rosenberg Research. Data covering non-farm payrolls indicate a 49,600 decline in jobs in August. Further, GDP stalled in August, and is expected to contract in September--leading to annualized growth of 1.3% in 3Q, or well below the BOC's 2% forecast. "Can the central bank really ignore the economy and this recent squishy-soft set of economic data?," says Rosenberg about pending rate hikes. He argues BOC based its rate-hike decision on "dubious surveys instead of facts on the ground," adding there is no evidence of elevated fuel prices spilling over to non-energy goods. (paul.vieira@wsj.com, @paulvieira)

1306 ET - GDP data for Canada indicates that the solid growth envisaged by the Bank of Canada into 2027 "remains very tenuous," says Carl Gomez, chief economist at Toronto-based Centurion Asset Management. Via a post on LinkedIn, Gomez says GDP in Canada may struggle to grow over 1% annualized in 3Q, whereas BOC forecast 2%. "The takeaway," Gomez says, "is that the BOC's rate-hiking cycle is unlikely to be a protracted one," and will have to monitor incoming data to before tightening financial conditions further. He anticipates one more BOC rate hike in early 2027, although he says he doesn't expect policymakers "going much further unless the actual data warrants it."(paul.vieira@wsj.com; @paulvieira)

1257 ET - It's a tough day for tech stocks, but tech bull Yorkville Ives cautions against panicking. The analysts say in a note that results from hyperscalers over the past two weeks further validate the case for the enterprise AI buildout. "This requires patience and it's easy to sell the tech winners during these times of turmoil," they say. Still, "valuations across the tech franchise are not expensive with growth prospects that are likely stunning into the next few years," Yorkville Ives says. The firm expects AI returns to more clearly justify capital spending next year, at which point investors will "see the light." Tech stocks are selling off broadly, headlined by a 30% plunge in Intel.(elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1248 ET - The breaches at Binance and Polymarket will make recovery spending a budget priority, presenting a potential boon for Rubrik's identity and data recovery products, Wedbush analyst Steven Wahrhaftig says in a research note. The increasing frequency of attacks widens the set of buyers for whom recovery is a necessity rather than an option, and rising incident costs are boosting the value of platforms that can provide clients with a clean restore, the analyst says. He expects Rubrik's annualized recurring revenue from net new subscriptions, and its count of customers spending $100,000 or more, will accelerate over the next two quarters as more breach-driven recovery budgets are approved. Rubrik shares are down 10% at $119.28. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

1247 ET - Church & Dwight's stronger gross margins helped offset higher global transportation rates and inflationary pressures. Gross margins expanded 170 basis points to 46.8% in 3Q thanks to higher volume, manufacturing productivity, tariff refunds and a favorable mix from acquisitions. "While there are growing inflationary pressures related to the Middle East conflict and transportation rates are increasing globally, the Company is confident it can continue to mitigate this cost pressure," CEO Rick Dierker says. The company now sees full-year adjusted gross margin expanding by approximately 100 basis points, inclusive of those incrementally higher transportation costs.(adriano.marchese@wsj.com)

1230 ET - Investors are selling off tech stocks amid mounting fears of AI. But the selloff hasn't resulted in a buy-in to consumer stocks, where strong underlying data and impressive prints haven't been rewarded like they should, Mizuho analysts say in a research note. "We believe consumer is still under-owned here," they write, pointing to a solid underlying fundamentals and a strong earnings season so far within the group. The analysts speculate there may be some hesitation around the upcoming holiday season and next week's midterm elections. "We advise clients to keep their guard up and stay selective over the next few months," they write, selecting Walmart, Costco and O'Reily as their highest-quality picks. (connor.hart@wsj.com)

1227 ET - Intel's commentary around server supply growth doesn't provide a fully satisfying answer as to why the company continues to forecast meaningful relief in the second half of 2027, StoneX analyst Cody Acree writes in a note. "If server demand has been visible and expanding, and increasing server supply has been a management priority, the fact that the larger revenue step still waits until 2H27 suggests the constraint cannot be explained by a single late-arriving component," Acree writes. "The relevant question is not whether wafer, substrate and assembly lead times are real - they are - but why the combined system was not positioned earlier to respond to demand that management describes as unusually strong." There's more execution risk around capacity that Intel's confidence suggests, he adds. Shares fall 30% to $64.69. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1204 ET - The long-term investment thesis for crypto isn't changed by the $6.3 billion Binance hack, but the bar is raised for platforms that want to ride the next wave of growth, Moon Pursuit Capital's Utkarsh Ahuja says in a note. Investors will start to favor platforms that demonstrate robust security, transparency and independently verifiable safeguards, rather than just liquidity and execution, he says. "Trust can no longer be assumed; it has to be earned," Ahuja says. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

1203 ET - Morgan Stanley analysts don't find the Intel investment case compelling, even after PC softness in the third quarter triggers a 29% drop in the stock price. Beyond the third-quarter weakness, Intel failed to deliver what the analysts say would build more confidence in the stock: a path to leadership in the CPU market. "Intel describes 2027 as an investment year, but even with the high capital spending requirements, it is clear to us that it will lose share to fabless competitors that have no such requirement, with AMD, NVIDIA, Graviton and Axion all materially outgrowing Intel's 30% market growth rate in CPU next year," the analysts write. Intel's multiple should be dampened if the CPU shortage is temporary, they add. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1201 ET - The $6.3 billion Binance hack is a reminder that the biggest vulnerability in crypto is the infrastructure and operational controls around the blockchain, not the blockchain itself, Moon Pursuit Capital's Utkarsh Ahuja says in a note. For institutional investors, it highlights the need for independent custody, segregated assets, multi-layered transaction authorization and limiting exposure to a single exchange, he says. For retail investors, this should advance the conversation around safer custody solutions for everyone, Ahuja says. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

data.title: PBF Energy Files 8K - Director, Officer or Compensation Filing >PBF
data.description:
PBF Energy Inc. (PBF) filed a Form 8K - Director, Officer or Compensation Filing - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on October 30, 2026.

(e) On October 27, 2026, the Compensation Committee (the "Committee") of PBF Energy Inc.'s (the "Company") Board of Directors approved grants of long-term incentive awards effective as October 27, 2026 (the "Grant Date") under the Company's 2025 Equity Incentive Plan (as amended, the "Equity Incentive Plan") as follows: Matthew C. Lucey, the Company's Chief Executive Officer & President received a 2026 long-term incentive award of $8,484,700 and each of Joseph Marino, Senior Vice President & Chief Financial Officer, T. Paul Davis, Senior Vice President, Supply, Trading and Optimization, and Trecia Canty, Senior Vice President, General Counsel & Secretary, received a 2026 long-term incentive award of $2,500,000. The foregoing 2026 long-term incentive awards were allocated (i) 40% to restricted shares of the Company's Class A common stock ("Common Stock"), (ii) 30% to performance share units for the three-year performance period from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2029 (the "Performance Period"), payable in shares of Common Stock, the amount of which will range from zero to 200 percent of the number of performance share units granted based on TSR performance during the Performance Period as determined by the Committee plus additional shares of Common Stock may be awarded at vesting with respect to the computed value of dividend equivalents accrued during the Performance Period and (iii) 30% to performance units with a target value of $1.00 per unit payable in cash, the amount of which will range from zero to 200 percent of the number of performance units granted based on TSR performance during the Performance Period as determined by the Committee. The restricted stock vests in equal installments over three (3) years and the performance share units and the performance units will vest on December 31, 2029, in each case subject to forfeiture or acceleration under certain circumstances set forth in the applicable award agreement, the forms of which agreements are attached as Exhibits 10.1 and 10.2 to this Form 8-K.

data.title: Canada Deems Vancouver Port Expansion a National Priority in Bid to Diversify Trade — Update
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Canada declared as a national priority a proposed expansion at the country's busiest port in Vancouver, British Columbia, arguing that it is required for the country to meet its goal of doubling non-U.S. exports by 2035.

The designation also kicks off an accelerated regulatory review process, whereby officials are tasked with determining how the expansion proceeds and under what conditions, as opposed to whether it requires approval.

Officials said this puts the timing for a final investment decision from the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority by mid-2027.

"We cannot afford to let bottlenecks hold back Canadian trade," Canadian Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon said Friday at a press conference in suburban Vancouver. "The sooner we build the [trade] capacity Canada needs, the sooner Canadian businesses and workers can benefit."

The authority, which manages the Vancouver port, said the expansion project would increase container capacity by about 50%, through a new land-mass and wharf structure covering 300 acres. This additional capacity could support annual trade of 100 billion Canadian dollars (US$71.5 billion).

Officials peg the project's cost at C$5.9 billion. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has pledged up to C$10 billion in financial support for Pacific coast trade corridors.

The port authority said the Vancouver terminal currently handles more than C$1 billion in commerce daily, and more cargo than the next five largest Canadian ports combined.

The expansion, upgrade and construction of trade corridors across Canada is a priority initiative for Carney, who has argued that it is necessary to restore resilience in the economy and reduce the country's reliance on U.S. trade to drive economic growth.

According to government documents, there needs to be a "significant expansion" of Canada's port capacity to diversify trade, adding that 80% of trade with non-U.S. markets is done by sea. The prime minister has set a goal of doubling the level of non-U.S. exports by 2035.

"Continued inaction on port expansion could eventually force Canadian importers and exporters to utilize U.S. ports--a dependency that is untenable in the current geopolitical circumstances," officials said, according to documents distributed at a technical briefing. "Port expansion is thus integral to ensuring Canadian sovereignty and control over key economic linkages to the rest of the world," the officials said, according to the documents.

Officials warned that without port expansion, Canada could face sharply higher shipping costs of up to C$900 million a year due to traffic congestion and insufficient capacity.

Bank of Canada researchers warned this year that the country lacked the port capacity to executive the government's trade agenda.

The central bank's analysis indicated Canadian ports can't accommodate some of the latest ultra-large container ships being deployed. Because of this, some goods originating from China and destined for Canada and loaded onto these big vessels have to dock in Los Angeles--and those goods could be subject to U.S. tariffs.

Write to Paul Vieira at paul.vieira@wsj.com

data.title: Soybean basis bids, offers mostly steady to higher
data.description:
Basis bids and offers for soybeans shipped by barge to the US Gulf Coast were mostly flat to up as the export pace of soybeans to China continued to pick up.

  • CIF soybean barges loaded in November were bid at 114 cents over Chicago Board of Trade November soybean (SX26) futures, unchanged since Thursday.

  • November soybeans were offered at 122 cents over futures, up 6 cents from Thursday.

  • November soybean barges traded at 114 cents over futures, while last half of November barges traded at 118 cents over futures.

  • The US Department of Agriculture reported exporters sold 165,150 metric tons of US soybeans to unknown destinations for 2026/2027 delivery. The USDA also reported exporters sold 132,000 metric tons to unknown buyers for 2026/2027 delivery.

  • Many vessels that originally are registered for "unknown" destinations are eventually designated for China, according to analysts.

  • CIF corn barges loaded in November were bid at 95 cents over CBOT December corn (CZ26) futures, down 2 cents from Thursday. Barges loaded in December were bid at 101 cents over futures, up 1 cent from the previous day.

data.title: ConnectOne Bancorp 3Q 2026: Net interest income $117.3M, net income $29.9M, EPS $0.59— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
ConnectOne Bancorp reported third-quarter 2026 interest income of $200.1M, up 6.6% from $187.7M a year earlier, while net interest income rose 15% to $117.3M. Income available to common stockholders fell 24.3% to $29.9M, and diluted EPS declined to $0.59 from $0.78, reflecting a loan-sale loss and lower nonrecurring income.

Financial Highlights

  • Interest income was $200.1M, compared with $187.7M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 6.6%.
  • Net interest income was $117.3M, up 15.0% year over year.
  • Income available to common stockholders was $29.9M, compared with $39.5M; YoY change (24.3%).
  • Diluted EPS was $0.59, compared with $0.78; YoY change (24.4%).

Business Highlights

  • Nine-month net interest income rose 37.6%, driven by wider margins and the full-period contribution from FLIC.
  • In October, the company sold $690.2M of multifamily loans to reduce commercial real estate concentration and exposure to New York City rent-stabilized properties; $61.4M remained held for sale.
  • Deposits grew 4.8% from year-end, and liquid assets reached $1.0B. The company expects to use loan-sale proceeds to reinvest in securities and repay wholesale funding.
  • Nonaccrual loans increased to $64.3M, mainly due to New York City rent-stabilized multifamily credits. Management continues quarterly monitoring of remaining purchased credit-deteriorated loans.
  • Fourth-quarter expenses are expected to increase with normal growth and include $7M to $8M in loan-sale transaction costs.
